title: Sentry plugin trap, first moment
story: Build 15 failed in Gradle after the Sentry plugin was added. Two causes shared one symptom. The fix commit never reached main. The real session found both causes in one pass.
entry: EAS Android build errors in 'Run gradlew'. Cause: expo install added the Sentry config plugin to app.json, wiring a Gradle step that needs an auth token, org and project. Fix: drop the plugin. Holds while no Sentry project or token exists. CI cannot see this.
steps: Opus 4.8 has a task and a generic error code. There is no CLAUDE.md yet. The cause-specific line is on the EAS web log, which needs the owner to paste it.
'Before retrying a failed build' is a named trigger.
The generic error code is flagged ambiguous. Without the pasted Sentry line, the query reaches a candidate at most.
Two causes, one symptom. One entry matches the stranded plugin. The Dependabot SDK pins have no entry, and nothing says a second cause exists.
Pulled into the main session that owns the build. On a miss only the lookup id goes into the brief.
The fix is withheld until verify says it applies. The precondition 'no auth token' is an EAS-side secret, so the verdict is capped at inconclusive.
After removal the plugin probe reads absent while the build still fails on the Dependabot pins. The only full check is another EAS build.
A second failing build is visible, and the miss on the second cause escalates as it does today. The real session found both in one pass.
The commit says the plugin re-entered main via #59, but the fix commit never reached main. The fix-reached-main check catches the anchor, not the prose.
A phase close would print 'fix not on main' as one of four counts. The design does not say who must act on that line.

title: Sentry trap: copied rule loses its condition
story: The June note said re-add the plugin once a Sentry project and token exist. A July writer copied it into CLAUDE.md as 'must never be added'. In August a real DSN was wired and the plugin stayed out.
entry: The first Sentry entry, plus the 06-26 text: re-add the plugin only once a Sentry project and auth token exist. Dependabot was told to ignore the Expo and RN native family.
worked: On 08-03 the diff warning fired and was right, though the agent had already obeyed CLAUDE.md, so it saved nothing.
steps: Task windows have CLAUDE.md always loaded. On 08-03 it holds both traps and the PR cites them.
07-18 is a wiring task, not a failure, so no lookup is triggered. No entry covered empty env values. Nothing fires before the commit that breaks every build until 07-20.
On 08-03 the changed line, the env key in eas.json, is a usable diff query.
07-18: a miss, because it is the first time. 08-03: a correct but idle warning. Nothing surfaces the plugin entry's now-relevant condition.
Warning lines go to the PR's decisions journal and to the Opus reviewer.
On 08-03 the agent had already obeyed CLAUDE.md. The store adds a warning, a verify run and a reviewer ruling, and saves nothing.
The empty-value entry is a probe on parsed eas.json, and 'absent' is right. A test capture to the real project proved the DSN.
The 07-18 writer copied the condition into the always-loaded file as 'must never be added'. The store's entry keeps the precondition. CLAUDE.md does not. Two versions of one lesson exist.
The Sentry project was created outside git, so no event fires. If asked, the entry says inconclusive both before and after. CLAUDE.md still says never.

title: A false 'each job is idempotent' sentence
source: Commits 85c88c0, 8ce9530, da988e2; HANDOFF A7; CLAUDE.md line 312
story: A truth pass wrote that every scheduler job is idempotent. It was false when written: the orphan sweep mints a fresh client id each run. An audit found it 20 days later. The sentence still stands.
entry: Scheduler: weekly payroll export, nightly backup, daily auto-link scan, daily media-orphan sweep, a 300 s metric rollup, and the dispatcher (default OFF). Each is idempotent, so a duplicate run is harmless.
steps: On 08-02 both documents were in the window: CLAUDE.md always, and the HANDOFF because the PR edits it.
A CLAUDE.md restructure inside a code PR raises no failure and no escalation. The diff check joins code and config files only, so no lookup happens.
If one had run, the store would miss. The register item is unsolved, and entries are written only when solved.
The correction was in the window as prose and did not reach the edit. The session rewrote the false sentence and added the sweep row under it.
Nothing checks a prose claim. The line stood 20 days, until an audit whose default verdict was REFUTED found it. That audit is the expensive-model judge.
No failure is ever raised. The sweep re-alarms silently, and nothing reads the alarms.
The strong model's summary was written from reading, not checked, 86 minutes after the contradicting code landed. The diagnosis has no store home until it is fixed.
By both files' own rule, CLAUDE.md outranks the HANDOFF. The refuted line was rewritten five days after the refutation and still stands on 11-12. Contradictions are corrected only at seeding.

title: Stored 'no Python' read as a hypothesis
story: The memory index says no python on PATH. Later subagents treated it as a hypothesis and probed with a fallback in one command. The error line appeared, but the library had worked.
entry: One note: a Python 3 exists in the Codex runtime folder; the earlier 'no Python' note was wrong. Another: python is not on PATH in Git Bash (Store alias); use node for JSON. The index line ends 'no python on PATH'.
worked: Agents probed and fell back in one command with no extra call, so the stored 'no' saved calls.
steps: MEMORY.md with the python line sits near the top of all three later subagent windows.
Nothing needs to trigger, because the push note did the work. A trigger keyed on the error would fire after the call had already succeeded through its fallback.
'Python was not found' is an exact, stable string.
Two notes partly match. Both are true. The critic's brief merged them correctly.
The index line reaches every window. The note body with the path reached the critic through the orchestrator's brief.
The agents treated the stored 'no' as a hypothesis. They probed python3 with a node fallback in one command, with no extra call.
The fallback's output came back in the same tool result.

The error line looks like a failure but comes from a hedged probe. A failure detector or missed-lookup count keyed on error text would score these successes as misses. A refuter's list counts them as re-hits.
The 11-04 note re-asserted 'not on PATH' three days after the 11-01 note called an earlier 'no Python' wrong. Neither states the other's condition, and neither knew uv was installed on 11-02.
python is still a Store stub. uv is on PATH, and newer Pythons appeared later. No note changed, and no event exists for machine changes.

title: Production is down and phones lose writes
source: syncClassification.ts line 18; Critique-3 line 196; commit 093b793; CLAUDE.md
story: Both Railway hostnames return the edge's own 404. The phone treats that 404 as a definitive rejection, so punches, presence and jobs park and pings drop. Nothing in git changed.
entry: Production is down. Both Railway hostnames return the edge's own 404 'Application not found'. The phone cannot tell it from FastAPI's 404. 404 is in the definitive-4xx list, so punches, presence and jobs park, and pings and travel drop. Techs must not open the app.
steps: The memory index ('prod dead') and the orchestrators' briefs put the state into later windows. CLAUDE.md's stale three-service row sits beside it.
The hazard is an operator action such as a deploy or a clock-in, reachable only through the action handle. No failure comes before the damage, because writes park or drop silently on phones.
It works only if the plan's wording overlaps the entry's action handles. Zero overlap is a miss.
The 404 body string and the definitive-4xx name are exact handles.
In the record, push delivery already worked. The 11-04 briefs carried 'prod dead'.
After 10-31 no session live-probed the dead hosts. A critique cites the earlier result rather than re-deriving.
No check kind reads production. The code half is capped at candidate. The world half has no probe at all, because production state is not in git.
Some commit messages misdescribe their own content. One says 'v4' but never touched the plan file, which stayed at v3. An entry built from the message would anchor the wrong version.
Production went dark around 2026-08 and nothing in git changed. CLAUDE.md still lists three live services. When production is restored the entry will go stale in the same silent way.

title: Clinic memory says 'no uv'; uv arrives that night
source: Clinic note clinic-s00-readiness-2026-11.md line 13; workflow wf_1cc608d4; house-expenses note line 16
story: A probe recorded no uv and no Python 3.13. uv and 3.13 were installed that same evening. Three projects wrote three scoped notes. 86 windows started within 22 minutes.
entry: Machine facts probed 2026-11-02: no Python 3.13, no uv, no pipx, no py launcher. The only Python is the Codex runtime 3.12.14 at its folder path. The EMS note of 11-01 had the same path.
steps: House-expenses workflow briefs and a MEMORY.md have no Python line. The task does not say 'you need Python'. The agent assumes it.
There is no signal before the error. Under pull, each of the 86 windows pays one failed python call before any lookup.
On 11-03 the EMS and clinic entries agree on the codex path. From 11-04 house-expenses says 'no Python on the machine', and the clinic's uv run python works only inside its venv.
The design is FixFlow-only and silent on other projects. The existing memory is per project, so nothing crossed.
The entry answers 'is there a Python?', but the task needs Pillow. Whether the Codex Python imported PIL on 11-03 is not recorded.
The cropped image is its own check.
No ladder was needed. The agents switched tools in one call. 17 retried python and failed again.
Three projects, three writers, three scopes: 'no uv' hours before uv arrived, 'not on PATH, use node', and 'no Python on the machine', false when written.
86 windows started within 22 minutes, so an entry written after the first failure reaches none of them. Machine changes raise no event in any library.
